# HealthKit

<!-- generated:header (isim/tools/coverage-summary.py; do not edit by hand) -->
**Symbols:** 42.1% of Apple's iOS API (844 of 2005, exact) · **Rows:** 20: 14 ✅ 2 🟡 4 ❌ · **iOS:** 8.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [Location, personal data & sensors](../COVERAGE.md#location) · **Apple:** [HealthKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit) · **Issues:** [`area:location`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Alocation)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** a JSON sample store (`isim/swift/overlays/HealthKit/Store.swift`) and the Health access sheet.
- **Workouts** (issue #418): workouts, their events, activities, statistics and routes are kept in the same database;
  `HKWorkoutBuilder` builds them on every iOS version, and from iOS 26 a workout session on iPhone collects a simulated
  exerciser's heart rate, energy and distance (`isim/swift/overlays/HealthKit/WorkoutBuilder.swift`).
- **The Health profile** (issue #419): the characteristics and the activity rings' goals are the device's
  (`isim health profile|goals`, [SCRIPTING.md](../SCRIPTING.md)); activity summaries are computed from each day's samples.
- **Objective-C / C interface:** headers in `isim/sdk-src/Frameworks/HealthKit` over the overlay's classes; not yet
  `HKStatisticsCollectionQuery` and `dateOfBirthComponents` (isim's Foundation has no `NSDateComponents`).

The samples go to the Health database like a watch's; pauses leave gaps. `recoverActiveWorkoutSession` returns the session running in the app. Tested (HelloWorkout: test_workout on iOS 26 and 27, `os_matrix`) |
